title: Introduction
subject: English
promptText:
Reading comprehension about greeting and Introduction. Provide a text followed by corresponding 5 questions.
There will be 5 text. The text can be dialog or monologue

questions.question: What is the main purpose of greeting someone?

options.B: To show respect and acknowledge their presence

questions.question: In the conversation between Tom and Jerry, why does Jerry ask about Tom's family?

options.B: To show interest and build rapport
options.C: To find out if Tom is rich

questions.text:
Tom: Hi Jerry, how are you today?
Jerry: I'm good, thanks. How about your family? Are they doing well?

In many cultures, asking about family is a common way to show interest and build rapport during conversations.

questions.question: What is the appropriate response to 'How do you do?'
questions.text: In formal introductions, when someone says 'How do you do?', it is customary to respond with the same phrase.

questions.question: According to the text, which of the following is NOT a common greeting in English?
questions.text: Common greetings in English include 'Hello', 'Hi', 'Good morning', 'Good afternoon', 'Good evening', and 'How are you?'. 'Goodbye' is used for farewell, not greeting. 'Please' is a polite word used to make requests, not a greeting.

questions.question: Why is it important to introduce yourself properly?

options.A: To impress others with your vocabulary
options.B: To establish your identity and start communication

questions.question: In the dialogue between Sarah and Mike, what does Mike mean when he says 'I'm between jobs right now'?

options.C: He is looking for a better job

questions.text:
Sarah: So Mike, what are you up to these days?
Mike: I'm between jobs right now. Just taking some time to find the right opportunity.

questions.question: What is the most appropriate way to introduce someone else?

options.A: This is John, he's my friend
options.C: I'd like you to meet John, he's my friend

questions.text: When introducing someone, you can use various phrases depending on the formality of the situation. All the options provided are acceptable ways to introduce someone.

questions.question: According to the text, which greeting is most appropriate for formal occasions?
questions.text: Formal occasions require greetings that show respect and maintain professional boundaries. Using titles like Mr., Mrs., Ms., or Dr. along with a proper greeting is appropriate for formal settings.

questions.question: In the conversation between Emma and Olivia, why does Emma apologize?
questions.text:
Olivia: I'm glad you could make it to the meeting.
Emma: I apologize for being late. The traffic was terrible.

questions.question: What should you do when someone introduces themselves?

options.A: Ignore them and look at your phone

questions.question: In the monologue about meeting new people, what does the speaker suggest about handshakes?

options.C: Handshakes are only for formal occasions

questions.text: When meeting new people, a firm handshake conveys confidence and respect. It should be firm but not bone-crushing, and should last about 2-3 seconds.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'How are you?' and 'How have you been?'?

options.B: How have you been? refers to a longer period
options.C: How are you? is more formal
options.D: How have you been? is only used with family

questions.text: 'How are you?' typically asks about the person's current state, while 'How have you been?' asks about their recent experiences over a longer period, such as since you last met.

questions.question: In the dialogue between David and Lisa, what does Lisa mean when she says 'I'm tied up at the moment'?
questions.text:
David: Hey Lisa, do you have time to talk about the project?
Lisa: I'd love to, but I'm tied up at the moment. Can we chat later this afternoon?

questions.question: According to the text, which of the following is a good way to end a conversation politely?

options.B: It was nice talking to you

questions.text: When ending a conversation, it's polite to give a reason for leaving and express appreciation for the interaction. This shows respect for the other person's time and the conversation you've had.

questions.question: What should you do when you forget someone's name after an introduction?
In the conversation between James and Maria, what does Maria mean when she says 'I'm new around here'?

options.A: She is new to the neighborhood
options.B: She is new to the country
options.C: She is new to the school

questions.text:
James: Welcome to our school! I hope you're settling in well.
Maria: Thanks! I'm new around here, so everything is still a bit overwhelming.

questions.question: What is the purpose of making eye contact during an introduction?
According to the text, which of the following is NOT a way to greet someone in the morning?
questions.text: Morning greetings include 'Good morning', 'Morning', and 'Hello'. 'Good night' is used in the evening or before bedtime, not as a morning greeting.

questions.question: In the dialogue between Kevin and Rachel, why does Kevin say 'It's a pleasure to meet you'?

options.B: He is genuinely happy to meet Rachel

questions.text:
Rachel: It's nice to meet you, Kevin.
Kevin: The pleasure is all mine. It's a pleasure to meet you too.

questions.question: What should you avoid when introducing yourself?
In the monologue about cultural greetings, what does the speaker say about bowing?

options.A: It is the most common greeting worldwide
options.B: It is appropriate in some cultures
options.C: It is only done by women

questions.text: Different cultures have different greeting customs. While handshakes are common in Western cultures, bowing is a traditional greeting in many Asian countries like Japan and Korea. The depth and duration of the bow can convey different levels of respect.

questions.question: What is the difference between a formal and informal introduction?
questions.text: Formal introductions typically include titles (Mr., Mrs., Dr.) and last names, while informal introductions use first names. Formal introductions often follow a more structured format and may include more details about the person's position or background.

questions.question: In the conversation between Anna and Ben, what does Ben mean when he says 'I'm in the same boat'?

options.B: He is in a similar situation

questions.text:
Anna: I'm so stressed about the exam tomorrow.
Ben: I know what you mean. I'm in the same boat. I haven't had enough time to study either.

questions.question: According to the text, what should you do when someone greets you in a language you don't understand?
questions.text: When someone greets you in a language you don't understand, it's polite to acknowledge them with a smile and a friendly greeting. If appropriate, you can ask them to repeat or explain what they said, showing interest in their language and culture.

questions.question: In the dialogue between Claire and Tom, why does Claire say 'I've heard so much about you'?

options.A: She has actually heard about Tom

questions.text:
Tom: Nice to meet you, Claire.
Claire: The pleasure is mine. I've heard so much about you from our mutual friends. They speak very highly of your work.
